recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If FHIR-I wants machine-readable reverse-chain discovery in the current build, handle it through a current tracker or proposal that specifies the concrete CapabilityStatement, SearchParameter, or extension semantics.
issue_request: FHIR-28534 was a Published FHIR-core change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification, asking how CapabilityStatement/SearchParameter can advertise reverse chaining (_has) support and recording that clients should not assume reverse chaining is supported wherever forward chaining is supported.
initial_application: The issue was applied by HL7/fhir#2145: f7b26fb added a CapabilityStatement note, and f1d3052 merged it. The application documented the discovery gap, the non-assumption rule, and open questions rather than adding a new CapabilityStatement or SearchParameter element.
additional_context: FHIR-I minutes from 2020-12-14 accepted the request while leaving open where and how to model reverse-chain support. FHIR-I minutes from 2022-08-08 recorded the implementation path as adding an STU paragraph in CapabilityStatement for reader comment. Current source still has that note; SearchParameter.chain remains forward-chain-only, and CapabilityStatement has include/revinclude/searchParam declarations but no field for supported _has combinations. Searches did not find a later final FHIR-core issue contradicting that applied approach.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Adding a machine-readable reverse-chain declaration now would be a new design decision beyond the evidence for this published R5 issue.

related_jiras.note: Mentioned in FHIR-28534 comments, but it concerns missing standard SearchParameter definitions and registry/tooling rather than reverse-chain capability declaration.
Later clarified search support declarations in the same CapabilityStatement/search area and is already represented separately on the combined branch.

evidence_items.learned: This establishes the final issue scope: clients should not assume _has support from forward-chain support, but the concrete declaration mechanism remained an open design question.

evidence_items.learned: The vote did not approve a concrete model element that could be safely added during reconciliation.

evidence_items.summary: FHIR-I recorded that FHIR-28534 would add an STU paragraph in CapabilityStatement to state options for reader comment.
evidence_items.learned: This confirms that the applied R5 source change was intentionally a note, not a new CapabilityStatement or SearchParameter field.

evidence_items.learned: The current source has direct history from the Jira-tagged application commit.

evidence_items.learned: The current source already conveys the approved applied content for FHIR-28534.

evidence_items.summary: CapabilityStatement exposes include/revinclude/searchParam declarations, while SearchParameter.chain describes forward chained names only.
evidence_items.learned: There is no missed mechanical reverse-chain field to populate; adding one would be new design work.

evidence_items.summary: CapabilityStatement and SearchParameter are active resources in the current FHIR build and assigned to FHIR-I.
evidence_items.learned: The inspected source files are in build scope for this reconciliation decision.
